summary:
Engineer "mesh", round 9. Started 05:30, last source change 06:10, last test 06:17 (47 minutes). Only src/js/46-mesh.js changed. Final page dist/r9-mesh.html (md5 61e2a46f05e9b3a864e4a6bd961b03ef); tools/smoke.json passes on it (52 steps, exit 0, no console errors). Notes: notes/r9-mesh.md. All runs under out/r9/mesh/ (v8/ = reference made before any change, r9-mesh/ = final build).

Item 1 (cut face rim): fixed for the starting offset and above, measured and seen. Shapes untouched (every STL byte-identical to v8). One case reads worse than v8 by my number: offset 0 (0.987 to 0.947), a thin coloured line round the face; not traced.
Item 2 (first model waits with no reason given): fixed. The progress line now says why for as long as the wait lasts. The wait itself is as long as before.
Item 3 (mesh-2, negative power): NOT cured, and measured that no offset cures it. 16 jobs on v8 (128/256/512 cells, offsets 0.5/1/1.5, every piece and largest only): best outline overlap 0.64; a larger offset lowers the overlap at every resolution. So no button and no new starting value; the warning now says what does help (untick "Keep only the largest piece", 256 or 512 cells) and that a larger offset makes thin parts thick. Ordinary solids get exactly what they got.
Item 4 (seven standard jobs before/after): all 7 STL identical to v8; 5 of 7 PLY identical; julia1-256 differs in 2 of 50,334 point colours; cut-128 differs on purpose.

Measured vs reasoned: all numbers above are measured. Reasoned only: the cause of the rim (from the code; the fix confirms it), the cause of the offset-0 line, and that item 2's code behaves the same on the final build as on the 06:03 build where its timeline was recorded (the code did not change; the smoke test's model job did run through it on the final build).
files_changed: out/r9/mesh/ (scripts, logs, pictures; includes 46-mesh.before.js and edit1.py to edit4.py, the four edits as applied)

fixed.id: item 1: cut face of a model keeps a coloured rim
fixed.what: meshPoint now colours a point of a cut face from a sample that holds the face's colour (inside end, else outside end, else nearest such sample within g.reach cells, else the last face colour found). A point is of the cut plane's face when its edge is upright, its outside end is above the face, and the cut plane is reached before the solid's own surface or the point sits within half a cell under the face. A surface point whose inside end holds the face colour takes the outside end's colour alone. Positions are untouched.
fixed.evidence: Measured, final build, out/r9/mesh/cmp-cutface-final.txt and cmp-standard-final.txt: share of the picture's plain cut face that is plain in the model, v8 to round 9: cutm-128 0.917 to 0.977; cutm-256 0.940 to 0.968; offset 2 0.784 to 0.982; Basilica 0.918 to 0.952; rabbit 0.915 to 0.973; tester's cut-128 0.906 to 0.965 (hue 7.1 to 6.3 deg). Offset 0: 0.987 to 0.947 (worse). All STL files byte-identical to v8. Seen: out/r9/mesh/sheet-cut-a.png, sheet-cut-b.png, sheet-cut-close.png.

fixed.id: item 2: first model of a formula waits about 3 s with nothing said
fixed.what: meshPrepare(job) runs before the first sample; while the renderer's program for volume samples is being prepared the progress line reads 'Preparing to read this solid. The first model of each formula takes a few seconds longer. The next one starts at once.' and adds 'N seconds so far.' from two seconds on. No percentage is shown with it. Cancel works during the wait.
fixed.evidence: Measured. v8 (out/r9/mesh/v8/log-first.txt): 'Starting. 0%.' for 6.2 s (Mandelbrot), 2.1 s (Kleinian), 5.9 s (power -2). My page (out/r9/mesh/r9-mesh/log-first.txt, build of 06:03): the sentence shown from 0.04 to 4.6 s, 0.16 to 2.5 s, 0.20 to 4.5 s; second job of each formula shows 'Finding the solid' at once. Whole jobs 6.4/4.6/7.0 s against 9.0/4.0/7.7 s on v8: the wait is unchanged within what a shared GPU does.

fixed.what: The warning for a solid that comes out as 200 pieces or more is one paragraph that says what helps, instead of two that did not. Largest piece kept: '... only the largest was kept: about 27% of the surface. So this model does not look like the picture. To get closer, untick "Keep only the largest piece" and choose 256 or 512 cells, then start again. A larger surface offset joins more of the pieces, but it makes the thin parts thick.' Every piece kept: names the next resolution and the same sentence on the offset. The mosaic warning is as it was.
fixed.evidence: Measured on the final build: out/r9/mesh/r9-mesh/log-warn.txt (power -2 at 128 default, 128 all pieces, 256 all pieces, mosaic at 128), no console errors.

fixed.id: item 4: the tester's seven standard jobs
fixed.what: Re-run on v8 and on the final build with the tester's scripts.
fixed.evidence: Measured, out/r9/mesh/cmp-standard-final.txt. Overlap and hue identical on both pages for mandel-128 (0.950; 3.3 deg, 97%), rabbit-128 (0.967; 2.8, 96%), julia1-128 (0.956; 7.3, 91%), julia1-256 (0.972; 4.7, 98%), klein-128 (0.960; 3.5, 91%), trapsolid-128 (0.965; 7.5, 86%); cut-128 0.945 on both, hue 7.1 to 6.3 deg, 83 to 85%. All closed and oriented, same triangles, volumes, sizes. STL identical for all 7; PLY identical for 5; julia1-256: 2 of 50,334 points changed colour by at most 20 of 255.

not_fixed.id: mesh-2 (major): a negative power gives a model that does not look like the picture
not_fixed.why: No setting of the mesher gives a model true to the picture. Measured on v8, out/r9/mesh/v8/check-neg.txt (overlap; picture's outline missing; model outside the picture): every piece kept: 128 cells 0.567/0.472/0.444 at offsets 0.5/1/1.5; 256 cells 0.641/0.529/0.480; 512 cells 0.628/0.545 at 1/1.5. Largest piece only: 0.157 to 0.440, with 16 to 82% of the picture missing. So I added no button and no starting value, as the assignment says for this outcome.
not_fixed.learned: With every piece kept the picture's own shapes are there from 256 cells on (discs on the spine, ball, wings), clearest at 512 with offset 1, but always inside complete outer shells that the picture draws only as thin arcs, so the model looks like a striped balloon with the picture's objects inside (out/r9/mesh/sheet-negpow-v8.png). A larger offset covers the picture's outline (under 1% missing) but thickens the shells, and overlap falls at every resolution. The largest piece is a spine with one or two loops at every setting. Round 7's finding stands: the picture's surface is a skin of 0.8 pixel that the samples do not carry. 512 cells at offset 0.5 was not run again (round 7: 0.64). Not shown by a number: that 512 follows the picture more closely than 256 at offset 0.5 (0.64 both); the warning's sentence at 256 cells rests on the pictures.

not_fixed.why: Found at 06:13 after the last build I could still test in full; changing the source again would have meant re-running everything past the stop time.
not_fixed.learned: At offset 0 the plain share of the cut face fell from 0.987 (v8) to 0.947: a thin line of surface colours round the face and a coloured needle (sheet-cut-close.png, lower row). v8 was pale there because it blended the face's cream into rim points. Reasoned, not tried: either wall points that now hold the full surface colour (MESH_FACE_RULE2), or rim points more than half a cell under the face; MESH_FACE_NEAR = 1 would settle the second. Going from 0.945 to 0.947 when MESH_FACE_NEAR was added suggests the first.

names_added: MESH_FACE_BELOW (1.01), MESH_FACE_ABOVE (3.01), MESH_FACE_DEEP (1.5): where a sample holds the cut face's colour; they repeat RAW_CUT, RAW_ABOVE, RAW_IN of 30-shaders.js
MESH_FACE_NEAR (0.5): a point this close under the cut plane's face, in cells, is coloured as part of it
MESH_FACE_RULE2 (true): a surface point whose inside end holds the cut face's colour takes the outside end's colour alone; kept as a switch
MESH_WORDS.prepare: the sentence of the progress line while the first model of a formula is prepared
meshTrue(g, lo, mid, hi): now returns { d, f, own }; own = the distances before the picture's limits are applied

meshSlice(g, d, c, end, f, own, zc): two new arguments; a slice now has .own, .zc (height above the cut plane, minus infinity without a cut), .wall (samples put outside by the wall of the grid), .face (every inside sample of this slice holds the cut face's colour)
meshHoldsFace(g, s, q): the sample holds the cut face's colour, not a surface colour
meshFaceFrom(g, si, qi, so, qo): the sample a point of a cut face takes its colour from, or null
g.reach, g.faceCol (grid object of meshBuild): how many cells meshFaceFrom looks (2 plus the offset, at most 8); the last face colour found
meshPrepare(job): waits while snapProg(job.snap, true) answers 'wait' and keeps the progress line saying so
job.plain: while set, meshPaint shows the step alone, without percentage or time left
meshRun locals fine, more; changed texts of #meshWarn for 200 pieces and more
No id, label, file name, state field, uniform or program-key flag was added or changed. src/css/46-mesh.css is untouched.
needs_from_others: src/body.html, 'How do I get a picture or a 3D model out?', sentence 'The first model of a formula takes a few seconds longer while it is prepared.' Still true; suggested: 'The first model of a formula takes a few seconds longer while it is prepared, and the progress line says so for as long as it lasts.'

src/body.html, same paragraph, 'One kind of solid does not come out like its picture yet: one made of sheets thinner than a cell of the grid, such as a negative power. The panel says so when it happens.' Still true; suggested ending: 'The panel says so when it happens, and what brings the model closer: untick Keep only the largest piece and choose 256 or 512 cells. Even then the model shows outer shells that the picture draws only in part.'

src/body.html, same paragraph, after 'Its colours are read from the surface the same way the picture's are; ...' add: 'A solid that is cut open gets the colour of the cut face there, right up to its edge.' (Holds from the starting offset 0.5 up; at offset 0 a thin coloured line remains.)

src/js/30-shaders.js (engine): if RAW_CUT, RAW_ABOVE or RAW_IN change, MESH_FACE_BELOW, MESH_FACE_ABOVE and MESH_FACE_DEEP in 46-mesh.js must follow, or the model's cut face gets surface colours again.

src/js/40-render.js (engine): meshPrepare calls snapProg(snap, true) and reads the answer 'wait'. Keep the name and that answer; if either changes the job still runs but the sentence is no longer shown (guarded by typeof).

Engine, mesh-2: round 7's request stands. A model true to the picture of a sheet solid needs the sampled estimate to carry the picture's own skin (the surface is drawn where the estimate reads 0.8 pixel).

Engine, painted cut face: in the middle of the face the model's 'How deep inside' colours differ from the picture's (11.1 deg median, 67% within 30; out/r9/mesh/sheet-cut-b.png, last row). That is the sample's colour, not the mesh.
measurements: Compile and drawing times: not measured. My change is in 46-mesh.js only, which holds no shader and draws no picture (reasoned). The first-model wait, which is the model program's compile, is unchanged: whole first jobs 6.4/4.6/7.0 s on my page against 9.0/4.0/7.7 s on v8 (Mandelbrot/Kleinian/power -2; out/r9/mesh/r9-mesh/log-first.txt, out/r9/mesh/v8/log-first.txt; GPU shared).

Smoke: tools/smoke.json on the final build, 52 steps, exit 0, no console errors, model job delivered squaring-lab-julia-48.zip (out/r9/mesh/smoke-final.log, 06:16). Also passed on the build before (out/r9/mesh/smoke-1.log).

Cut face, share of the picture's plain face that is plain in the model, v8 to final (out/r9/mesh/cmp-cutface-final.txt): cutm-128 0.917 to 0.977; cutm-256 0.940 to 0.968; cutm-128 offset 0 0.987 to 0.947; offset 2 0.784 to 0.982; cutj-128 0.918 to 0.952; cutr-128 0.915 to 0.973; cut-128 0.906 to 0.965. Painted face cutp-128: hue 12.6 to 11.1 deg, 63 to 67% within 30.

Standard jobs v8 = final unless noted (out/r9/mesh/cmp-standard-final.txt): mandel-128 overlap 0.950, hue 3.3 deg 97%; rabbit-128 0.967, 2.8, 96%; julia1-128 0.956, 7.3, 91%; julia1-256 0.972, 4.7, 98%; cut-128 0.945, 7.1 to 6.3 deg, 83 to 85%; klein-128 0.960, 3.5, 91%; trapsolid-128 0.965, 7.5, 86%. All 7 STL byte-identical; all closed and oriented.

Built-in fields through the panel on the final build (out/r9/mesh/fields-r9-mesh.txt): 10 of 10 runs give the same triangles, points, pieces, Euler number and volume as round 7 (out/r7/mesh/fields-r7-mesh.txt); no console errors.
No console errors in any drive run (log-first, log-cutface, log-warn, log-standard under out/r9/mesh/r9-mesh/).
sheets: out/r9/mesh/sheet-cut-a.png: picture, v8 model, round 9 model of the cut Mandelbrot solid at 128, 256, offset 0 and offset 2. Look at the rim of the face: rainbow band in the middle column, cream to the edge on the right; third row (offset 0) shows the thin coloured line that is left.

out/r9/mesh/sheet-cut-close.png: the needle end three times enlarged. Top row: blue needle in v8, cream in round 9, as in the picture. Bottom row: offset 0, where v8 is paler and mine has a coloured needle.

out/r9/mesh/sheet-cut-b.png: Basilica, rabbit, and the painted cut face. In the last row the rim is pink like the picture's instead of trap colours; the middle of the face still differs from the picture (engine side).

out/r9/mesh/sheet-negpow-v8.png: the power -2 picture (first tile) and eleven models. Second tile is what v8 gives by default; compare '256, 0.5, all' and '512, 1, all' (the picture's shapes inside outer shells) with '128, 1, all' and the three 'largest' tiles.
risks: Offset 0 on a cut solid shows a thin coloured line round the face where v8 was pale (0.987 to 0.947). Not traced.
A surface that passes within half a cell under the cut plane without being cut is coloured as the face (reasoned, not run): a ring up to about one cell wide on a dome cut near its top.
Three numbers in 46-mesh.js repeat constants of 30-shaders.js, which the other engineer is editing this round. If those change, the model's cut face silently gets surface colours again.
meshPrepare depends on snapProg in 40-render.js, also being edited this round. If its name or its 'wait' answer changes, the sentence silently disappears; the job itself still runs.
Item 2's timeline was recorded on the build of 06:03, not on the final one. The code of that item did not change after, and the smoke test's model job went through it on the final build.

Not run: offsets above 2 cells (above 3 the face's slices are no longer ones the sampler marks, so the face falls back to deep samples or the last face colour); a solid that runs into the wall of the grid (follows the new rule, no scene of mine does it); a solid cut by the drawing radius (as it was); the Kleinian view or a trap solid cut open; 192, 384, 512 cells for the standard jobs; a model made from the 2D view; files opened in Blender, Rhino or a slicer.
The warning at 256 cells says 512 follows the picture more closely; at offset 0.5 the overlap is 0.64 for both. v8's text made the same claim.
tools/smoke.json writes its screenshots to out/smoke-*.png, shared paths outside my folder; that is the tool's doing and I ran it twice.
